title: Hudson Pacific continues major upgrades at Bentall Centre
summary: Hudson Pacific Properties is proceeding with significant renovation plans at its Bentall Centre property in downtown Vancouver, adapting to COVID-19 by focusing on creating pandemic-friendly work environments. The upgrades aim to attract and retain employees, especially in the growing tech sector, and include new cycling facilities, outdoor plaza areas, and a rooftop dog park. Major tenants like Shopify and WeWork are maintaining their presence, and the complex remains 97 percent leased, with Hudson Pacific also assisting its 32 retail tenants through the Canada Emergency Commercial Rent Assistance program.

title: IonQ Unveils World's Most Powerful Quantum Computer
summary: IonQ has revealed its next-generation quantum computer, featuring 32 "perfect qubits" and an expected quantum volume exceeding 4,000,000. This new system, which boasts improved fidelity and is built on decades of research, will be available through Amazon Braket and Microsoft's Azure Quantum. IonQ aims to significantly increase its qubit count annually, with two more generations of hardware already in development.

title: Introducing the World’s Most Powerful Quantum Computer
summary: IonQ has unveiled its new quantum computer, which is described as the most powerful on the market, featuring 32 perfect qubits and a quantum volume of at least 4,000,000. This development validates IonQ's trapped-ion approach and positions quantum computing as the next major technological revolution, with the potential to transform numerous industries and create trillions in economic value. The system will initially be available to partners via private beta, then commercially on AWS Braket and Microsoft Azure Quantum in early 2021, aiming to accelerate the adoption and development of quantum applications.

title: The Most Popular ESG ETF is also a Five-Star Fund
summary: The iShares ESG Aware MSCI USA ETF (ESGU), a five-star rated fund by CFRA, is highlighted for its strong record and appealing holdings. Despite excluding some companies based on ESG criteria, ESGU has outperformed the S&P 500 Index over various periods and maintains a sector exposure similar to the broader market. CFRA recommends ESGU for investors seeking ESG-focused strategies, citing its low expense ratio and growing popularity.

title: All of 'Mad Men' Available on AMC Plus
summary: All seven seasons of the AMC hit drama "Mad Men" are now available commercial-free on AMC Plus, AMC Networks’ new streaming bundle. The streaming service also features original programming from AMC, IFC, BBC America, WE TV, and SundanceTV, including shows like "The Walking Dead" and "Killing Eve." AMC Plus is accessible to subscribers of Amazon Prime Video Channels, Apple TV Channels, Comcast Xfinity, Dish, and Sling TV, with pricing set at $8.99 monthly for some providers.

title: Walmart to revamp 1K stores with digital in mind
summary: Walmart plans to overhaul 1,000 of its stores by the end of its next fiscal year, introducing a new concept focused on a digitally-enabled shopping experience. These remodels will include new signage to encourage app usage, improved navigation designed like airports, self-checkout kiosks, and contactless payment systems. The initiative further integrates Walmart's online and in-store operations, coinciding with the launch of its Walmart+ membership service.

title: Amazon Timestream time series database generally available
summary: AWS has announced the general availability of Amazon Timestream, a serverless time series database designed to handle chronologically ordered data efficiently. This service emerged from a two-year preview, with improvements driven by customer feedback. Amazon Timestream integrates with other AWS services for event streaming and analysis and offers scalability for storage and query processing.

title: Elon Musk thought there was a 'greater than 90% chance both SpaceX and Tesla would be worth $0'–now he's the richest person in the world
summary: Elon Musk, now the wealthiest person globally, once believed there was over a 90% chance both SpaceX and Tesla would fail. Despite these initial doubts and significant financial risks, Musk personally invested millions to build both companies. Both SpaceX and Tesla overcame near bankruptcies and formidable obstacles to achieve monumental success, with Tesla becoming the world's most valuable automaker and SpaceX making strides in space exploration.

title: IonQ Unveils New 32-Qubit Quantum Computer
summary: IonQ has unveiled a new 32-qubit quantum computer with low gate errors, expecting a quantum volume greater than 4,000,000. This new system features perfect atomic clock qubits and random access all-to-all gate operations, and will be available via private beta before commercial release on Amazon Braket and Microsoft's Azure Quantum. IonQ plans to continue rapidly increasing qubit count and improving fidelity, with two new generations of hardware already in development.

title: Walmart’s U.K. Retreat Leaves Asda With New Owners, Old Problems
summary: Walmart Inc. has sold a controlling stake in its U.K. supermarket chain Asda to TDR Capital and the Issa brothers, marking its retreat from the U.K. retail market. This move leaves Asda with new owners, who are expected to bring entrepreneurial flair, but also faces long-standing challenges in the competitive U.K. supermarket business against established players like Tesco and J Sainsbury. The 1999 acquisition of Asda by Walmart was initially seen as a major disruptor to the market.

title: Larry Ellison's TikTok bid puts Oracle chairman back in the spotlight
summary: Oracle Corp. co-founder Larry Ellison's pursuit of a deal with TikTok could significantly boost Oracle's cloud-computing business and put him back in the tech industry spotlight. The proposed deal involves Oracle and Walmart Inc. taking a combined 20% stake in a new U.S.-based TikTok, with Oracle guaranteeing the security of U.S. user data. This move is seen as a way for Oracle to gain traction against market leaders like Amazon and Microsoft in the cloud computing sector, an area Ellison once dismissed.

title: Academy Sports Reaches ‘Inflection Point’ As IPO Debuts
summary: Academy Sports + Outdoors debuted its IPO below expectations, but CEO Ken Hicks remains confident in long-term success, citing the retailer's business reaching an "inflection point." The company has implemented a new strategy focusing on localized assortments, improved omnichannel capabilities, and benefiting from increased outdoor activity during the COVID-19 pandemic. Hicks believes these changes, along with its value-retailer positioning and broad customer base, will drive continued growth and differentiate Academy from competitors like Dick's Sporting Goods.

title: Shaking Up Aging in Place
summary: The Home Depot has launched a new "Independent Living" program in partnership with National Seating & Mobility (NSM) to cater to the growing senior market wishing to age in place. The program offers in-home consultations and installation services for accessibility modifications like ramps, stairlifts, and grab bars, initially rolling out in select New Jersey and Missouri stores. This initiative aims to address the significant demand for home modifications as a large percentage of the aging population prefers to remain in their current homes.

title: Mayor: New investment helping border recover from economic blow of COVID-19
summary: El Paso Mayor Dee Margo announced a new $150 million distribution facility from TJX Companies, which will create 950 jobs. This investment, along with a previously announced Amazon fulfillment center, is seen as crucial for the city's economic recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic. Regional leaders are also actively working to attract multinational companies from Asia to relocate their manufacturing operations to the Borderplex area, capitalizing on reshoring opportunities and emphasizing the skilled workforce and strategic location.

title: TJX Cos. to open $150M distribution center in El Paso
summary: TJX Cos., parent company of T.J. Maxx and Marshalls, is building a 1.6 million-square-foot distribution center in El Paso, Texas, with an initial investment of $150 million. This facility is expected to create 950 jobs over five years and will handle up to 240 inbound and outbound truck shipments daily. The decision to locate in El Paso was influenced by its proximity to the U.S.-Mexico border and growing reshoring opportunities from Asia.

title: The Honest Company's disinfectant spray is back in stock online
summary: The Honest Company's disinfectant spray is back in stock online and its hand sanitizer is at its lowest price ever, according to SFGate. The disinfectant kills 99.9% of germs and cold/flu viruses without harsh chemicals, while the hand sanitizer in Coastal Surf is available for $2.33. This comes after the release of The Honest Company's "Stay Safe" collection.

title: Pacific Biosciences Launches The Sequel IIe System To Accelerate Adoption Of Highly Accurate HiFi Sequencing
summary: Pacific Biosciences has launched the Sequel IIe System, an evolution of its SMRT Sequencing technology. This new system offers increased computational capacity and on-instrument data processing, allowing for faster and more cost-effective generation of highly accurate HiFi reads. The Sequel IIe System is designed to reduce data analysis time, transfer, and storage needs, making HiFi sequencing more accessible for various genomic and transcriptomic research projects.

title: EPAM Helps Bacardi Accelerate Digital Marketing and E-Commerce Transformation
summary: EPAM Systems partnered with Bacardi to revamp its digital marketing technology ecosystem, launching a new end-to-end, automated DevOps platform. This transformation, leveraging EPAM's AWS expertise, enabled Bacardi to significantly improve brand consistency, accelerate time-to-market for e-commerce solutions, and reduce operational costs, especially crucial as consumer buying behaviors shifted online due to COVID-19. The project enhanced consumers' search-to-checkout experience across Bacardi's digital portfolio.

title: Mattel Unveils Susan B. Anthony Barbie Doll as Newest Addition to Inspiring Women Series
summary: Mattel has released a Susan B. Anthony Barbie doll as the newest addition to its Inspiring Women Series, honoring Anthony's pivotal role in the women's suffrage movement. The doll features a historically accurate design and aims to celebrate her efforts which led to the 19th Amendment. This initiative is part of Barbie's broader Dream Gap Project, which seeks to recognize influential female figures and encourage girls to aspire to their full potential.

title: Teens are buying fewer clothes, less food as their spending hits two-decade low
summary: Teen spending dropped to a 20-year low during the coronavirus pandemic, with significant reductions in spending on apparel, food, and entertainment. According to Piper Sandler's "Taking Stock with Teens" report, annual spending fell by 9% year over year, as economic uncertainty led nearly half of teens to believe the economy was worsening. Despite the overall decline, Nike maintained its top spot in apparel and footwear, and Amazon remained the preferred online shopping destination.

title: Apple pulls rival products from stores ahead of launch
summary: Apple Inc. has removed rival products from its retail and online stores ahead of the anticipated launch of its new iPhone, speakers, and headphones. This strategic move impacts brands like Bose Corp., Sonos Inc., and Logitech International SA, and is a recurring practice for Apple, previously seen when it launched the Apple Watch in 2014. The company stated this is part of its regular curation of third-party accessories to complement its own products.

title: Former Speedway Exec's New C-Store Acquisition Venture Closes $200 Million IPO
summary: Recharge Acquisition Corp., a special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC) led by former Speedway LLC CEO Tony Kenney, has successfully closed a $200 million IPO. The company aims to acquire convenience-store chains, focusing on those with substantial scale and well-located fuel and convenience stores. The leadership team, including Kenney, views the fragmented c-store market as ripe for consolidation, targeting regional chains initially and then smaller acquisitions.

title: GE to close its Additive Pittsburgh facility at Chapman-Westport
summary: GE is closing its Additive Pittsburgh research facility at Chapman-Westport, which had only opened four years prior. The industrial giant is consolidating its additive manufacturing operations to Cincinnati. This move comes amid a struggling aviation industry, presenting challenges for manufacturers.

title: IonQ Releases A New 32-Qubit Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer With Massive Quantum Volume Claims
summary: IonQ has released its 5th generation 32-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer, claiming an astounding quantum volume of 4 million, significantly higher than previously published records. While the company calculated this figure rather than running quantum volume circuits, they anticipate a research paper confirming the performance. This development marks a significant advancement in quantum computing, with plans for private betas and cloud platform deployment in 2021.

title: Amazon and American Express extend relationship to launch new business credit cards in the UK
summary: Amazon and American Express have introduced two new small business credit cards in the UK: the Amazon Business Prime American Express Card and the Amazon Business American Express Card. These cards offer various benefits, including Amazon Rewards points and flexible payment terms, to support small businesses in managing their finances and growth. This initiative is part of Amazon's ongoing commitment to helping small businesses thrive in the UK, especially given current economic challenges.

title: Enhancing Serverless Security with Check Point CloudGuard and AWS Lambda Extensions
summary: This article discusses how Check Point CloudGuard and AWS Lambda Extensions enhance serverless security. It highlights the inherent security improvements with serverless computing due to a minimal attack surface and shared responsibility model, while still emphasizing the need for robust visibility, posture management, and application security. The integration of CloudGuard with AWS Lambda Extensions enables deeper monitoring and protection of serverless functions by analyzing application activity, remediating posture issues, and providing customized defense strategies.

title: Private equity giant Blackstone set to open tech office in Miami
summary: Private equity firm Blackstone plans to open a technology-focused headquarters in Miami, creating up to 215 tech jobs with an average salary of $200,000. Miami-Dade County will provide up to $650,000 in job incentives, anticipating $910,303 in new tax revenue. This move signifies Miami's growing appeal as a tech hub, attracting other companies like Google, Microsoft, and Softbank.

title: Office Stationery And Supplies B2B Market to Reach $29.14 bn by 2024, 3M Co., Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., Amazon.com Inc., and WHSmith Plc., Emerge as Key Contributors to Growth | Technavio
summary: The office stationery and supplies B2B market is projected to grow by USD 29.14 billion from 2020-2024, with a CAGR of almost 3%. Key market drivers include the increasing demand for recyclable stationery products and the growing online sale of office stationery and supplies. Major contributors to this growth include 3M Co., Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., Amazon.com Inc., and WHSmith Plc., with APAC expected to contribute 36% of the market share.

title: Ford to keep office workers at home through at least next June
summary: Ford Motor Co. has announced that its North American white-collar workers will continue to work from home through at least June of next year, extending a policy put in place at the start of the coronavirus pandemic. This decision mirrors similar extended remote work plans by other major companies like General Motors, Rocket Companies, Google, Facebook, and Amazon, as COVID-19 cases continue to rise across the U.S. By the time these policies expire, many employees will have been working remotely for approximately 15 months.

title: Village Super Market closes out fiscal 2020 on up note
summary: Village Super Market reported strong sales growth for fiscal 2020, with a significant 19.9% jump in sales for the fourth quarter driven by increased customer demand during the COVID-19 pandemic and strategic acquisitions. Online sales surged 240% in the fourth quarter and 83% for the full year. Despite a slight dip in reported net income for the full year, adjusted earnings also declined, though the company benefited from various one-time gains.

title: New Consumer Alert on Yelp Takes Firm Stance Against Racism
summary: Yelp has introduced a new "Business Accused of Racist Behavior Alert" to caution consumers about businesses associated with overtly racist actions, linking to news articles for more information. This initiative comes in response to a surge in reviews mentioning racist behavior and increased user interest in supporting Black-owned businesses. Yelp also partners with Open to All® to provide resources for small businesses aiming to create inclusive environments.

title: Foreign cloud service providers led by Amazon, MS play big in Korea
summary: Foreign cloud service providers, spearheaded by Amazon Web Services and Microsoft, are increasingly dominating South Korea's cloud computing market, capturing over half of it in 2019. Their aggressive expansion and investment in data centers in Korea are leading to higher growth rates compared to domestic providers. This trend is pushing local companies like Naver and Kakao to step up their own cloud infrastructure development and services.

title: Amazon Prime Day 2020: What to know about the online sales event
summary: Amazon Prime Day 2020, postponed due to the pandemic, is scheduled for October 13-14 and is expected to generate $9.9 billion worldwide. The event will focus on helping consumers save money during an economic downturn and supporting small businesses, potentially impacting Black Friday sales. Shoppers can anticipate deals on Amazon devices, appliances, electronics, clothing, and beauty products.

title: Parcel shipments passed 100B in 2019, will more than double by 2026: Pitney Bowes
summary: Global parcel volume reached 103 billion in 2019, driven largely by China, and is projected to more than double to 220-262 billion by 2026 due to e-commerce growth. Despite an e-commerce boom during the pandemic, carriers faced challenges like service interruptions and depressed economic activity, with some responding by implementing volume-control measures and price hikes to ensure profitability as volume growth outpaces revenue growth.

title: Amazon Prime Day is cash haul for Bezos backed e-commerce giant
summary: Amazon Prime Day 2020 was projected to generate nearly $10 billion in sales, a significant increase from previous years, despite being delayed due to the pandemic. The event, which requires an Amazon Prime membership to participate, serves as an early kickoff to the holiday shopping season and is a major sales period for the company, surpassing Black Friday and Cyber Monday combined. Amazon's stock saw an 86% gain that year, further enriching Jeff Bezos, the company's largest individual shareholder.

title: Peloton rolling out "Skip Intro" feature
summary: Peloton is introducing a "Skip Intro" feature for experienced riders, allowing them to bypass the minute-long class introductions. This feature will be available on Peloton hardware and the web, but not on their apps, and requires users to have completed at least five cycling classes to unlock it. The update aims to improve the workout experience for those already familiar with Peloton's interface and class structure.

title: Amazon Prime Day steals rivals’ Black Friday spotlight
summary: Amazon's two-day Prime Day event, delayed to October in 2020, is expected to give the e-commerce giant a significant advantage over brick-and-mortar stores. The annual sale is positioning itself to kick off the holiday shopping season early, fueled by pandemic-spooked consumers wary of Black Friday crowds and a general shift to online shopping. Analysts predict record online spending for Amazon, with the company's delivery infrastructure providing both convenience and safety during the ongoing pandemic.

title: Drones deliver COVID-19 tests in Cheektowaga based demo project
summary: A demo project in Cheektowaga, New York, is testing drone delivery of COVID-19 test kits to homes within a one-mile radius of a Walmart pharmacy. Droneup, in partnership with Walmart and Quest Diagnostics, is using FAA-certified pilots to navigate various weather conditions and proximity to an airport, demonstrating a method to deliver tests without people needing to leave their homes. This initiative aims to safely provide diagnostic access while minimizing community contact.

title: Spike in Amazon phishing for Prime Day: a new day of deals means new phishing campaigns
summary: This article warns about a significant increase in Amazon phishing schemes leading up to Prime Day, with cybercriminals leveraging the event to steal login credentials and credit card details. Attackers are using sophisticated tactics, including convincing email lures about account holds or expired Prime memberships, employing newly registered domains, and abusing legitimate services like Sniply to host malicious content. The report highlights two main types of scams ("Your Amazon Account's On Hold - Update Payment Info" and "Your Amazon Prime Membership Has Expired") and provides detailed analysis of the attack vectors, emphasizing the need for advanced email security solutions to combat these evolving threats.

title: Nuvemshop, a Latin American answer to Shopify, raises $30 million
summary: Nuvemshop, a Latin American e-commerce platform similar to Shopify, has raised $30 million in venture capital funding to expand its business. The company, operating as Nuvemshop in Brazil and Tiendanube elsewhere, supports 65,000 businesses and processes over $100 million in sales monthly. With this new funding, Nuvemshop plans to launch its own payment processing and logistics gateway, expand its app store, and offer broader financial services, including lending based on revenue.

title: Walmart, Target holding major sales this week to compete with Amazon Prime Day
summary: Walmart and Target are initiating major sales events this week to compete directly with Amazon Prime Day. Target's "Deal Days" run Tuesday and Wednesday, signaling an early start to holiday sales, while Walmart's "Big Save Event" offers Black-Friday-like discounts through Thursday. These events coincide with Amazon Prime Day, which was delayed this year and features a new "Watch This Deal" button for customer alerts.

title: Takeda to transform into a 'cloud-first company' through Accenture, AWS partnership
summary: Takeda is embarking on a five-year initiative, with the help of Accenture and Amazon Web Services, to become a "cloud-first company." The goal is to equip all scientists with cloud-based research tools and move 80% of drug development applications to the cloud within a decade, significantly reducing reliance on internal data centers. This transformation aims to accelerate decision-making through AI and streamline processes, as demonstrated by their quick launch of a data-sharing platform for clinical trials.

title: Amazon’s Prime Day Steals Rivals’ Black Friday Spotlight
summary: Amazon's delayed Prime Day in October is set to kick off the holiday shopping season early, giving the e-commerce giant a significant advantage over brick-and-mortar rivals as consumers prioritize online shopping due to pandemic concerns. Analysts predict record sales for Amazon, with online spending expected to reach nearly $10 billion during the two-day event, further solidifying the "Christmas creep" phenomenon. Despite a weak job market, Amazon's delivery model offers safety and convenience, leading to continued double-digit sales growth.

title: JBG Smith, Parking Management to settle lawsuit over parking fees
summary: Parking Management (PMI) will pay JBG Smith $1.45 million to settle a lawsuit regarding parking fees. This settlement comes after PMI sought Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection earlier in the year. The dispute involved funds from parking facilities managed by PMI for JBG Smith, including those in Crystal City, where Amazon's second headquarters is located.

title: Apple Announces First 5G Smartphone, iPhone 12
summary: Apple has announced its first lineup of 5G-enabled smartphones, the iPhone 12 series, which includes four models: the iPhone 12, iPhone 12 Mini, iPhone 12 Pro, and iPhone 12 Pro Max. While these new phones support 5G technology for faster wireless speeds, the full benefits may not be immediately available to all users as 5G networks are still under construction in many regions. Aside from the phones, Apple also revealed a smaller, more affordable HomePod Mini smart speaker.
source: VOA - Voice of America English News

title: Macy’s provides customers with luxury of same-day delivery
summary: Macy's is partnering with DoorDash to offer same-day and next-day delivery services from over 500 Macy’s and Bloomingdale’s locations across 47 states. This collaboration leverages DoorDash's white-label fulfillment service, DoorDash Drive, to fulfill digital orders without minimums or time slots. The partnership aims to provide customers with more convenient and faster shopping options, especially during the holiday season.

title: Ninth area facility identified for Amazon.com
summary: Amazon.com is expanding its presence in Jacksonville with a new 477,946-square-foot package delivery hub in North Jacksonville, its ninth identified facility in Northeast Florida. The city issued a permit for Threecore LLC to build-out the $15 million warehouse at 250 Busch Drive E., which will serve as a package delivery service employing workers across multiple shifts. This expansion continues Amazon's significant investment in logistics infrastructure in the region, with several other fulfillment and delivery centers already operational or under construction.

title: Bezos said warming is ‘biggest threat.’ Then he helped GOP
summary: Jeff Bezos, CEO of Amazon, publicly stated that climate change is the biggest threat to the planet, yet his personal political contributions and Amazon's PAC donations largely went to Republican senators who have opposed climate legislation. This pattern of donations to climate-skeptic lawmakers has drawn criticism and raises questions about the consistency of Amazon's stated climate commitments with its political spending. The article highlights a broader issue of corporations making climate pledges while financially supporting politicians who undermine those goals.

title: Using Factors As a Magnifying Glass for Equities | MSCI
summary: This article explains how factors, such as value and momentum, can be used as a "magnifying glass" to understand the characteristics and drivers of individual stocks and equity portfolios, even within seemingly similar peer groups. Using MSCI FaCS, the analysis reveals significant differences in factor exposures for high-profile tech companies, airlines, and even mutual funds categorized as "growth" funds. The article highlights the utility of factors for institutional investors in due diligence, portfolio analysis, and communicating investment objectives.

title: Zillow Group appoints Hines exec Claire Cormier Thielke to board
summary: Zillow Group has appointed Claire Cormier Thielke, a managing director at Hines, to its board of directors. Thielke's experience is expected to help Zillow in its transformation into a comprehensive real estate services provider. This move comes as Zillow prepares to launch its own brokerage in 2021.

title: Some Amazon HQ2 workers could work from home until summer 2021
summary: Amazon has informed some employees at its HQ2 in Arlington that they can continue working remotely until summer 2021. This decision could negatively impact local businesses that were anticipating increased patronage from Amazon employees. The company's development plans for the first two HQ2 buildings in Metropolitan Park, Arlington County, have been submitted.

title: Macy’s is turning stores dark for the holidays
summary: Macy's is converting two of its department stores into "dark stores" for the holiday season, focusing on online order pickup and returns rather than in-store shopping. This pilot program in Dover, DE, and Littleton, CO, aims to leverage increased online sales, which jumped 53% in Q2 while in-store sales declined significantly. The move is seen by many industry experts as a short-term solution to adapt to changing consumer behavior and utilize underperforming physical assets during the pandemic.

title: How to Switch from AWS EBS to Cloud Volumes ONTAP for LVM Storage
summary: This article explains how to migrate LVM storage from AWS EBS to Cloud Volumes ONTAP with zero downtime. It provides an overview of LVM, Cloud Volumes ONTAP, and a practical demonstration of the migration process using iSCSI. The article highlights the benefits of using Cloud Volumes ONTAP for data management, including advanced features like snapshots, data compression, and high availability.

title: Pitney Bowes Study: Global Parcel Volume Exceeds 100B for First Time Ever
summary: A new study by Pitney Bowes found that global parcel volume surpassed 100 billion in 2019, reaching 103 billion, with China generating more than three of every five parcels in major markets. The report forecasts that parcel volume is likely to more than double to 220-262 billion parcels by 2026, with a 14.8% CAGR for 2020-2024. Amazon Logistics was noted as a significant player, delivering 1.9 billion packages in the U.S. and showing 155% growth in 2019.

title: Amazon Announces Two New Fulfillment Centers in Kansas
summary: Amazon announced plans to open two new one million square-foot fulfillment centers in Kansas, creating over 1,000 new, full-time jobs. These facilities will handle bulky customer items, and Amazon also plans to open a new delivery station in Wichita. Governor Laura Kelly praised the investment, highlighting the state's workforce and economy, while Amazon reiterated its commitment to competitive pay, comprehensive benefits, and community investment.

title: HDFC Bank Partners with Amazon for GREAT INDIAN FESTIVAL Sale
summary: HDFC Bank has announced its partnership with Amazon for the upcoming Great Indian Festival Sale. This collaboration aims to offer various benefits and services to customers during the sale event.

title: ICICI Bank faces 'technical issue', online transactions fail
summary: ICICI Bank customers experienced significant issues with online transactions, including problems receiving OTPs for UPI payments and inability to process card payments. The technical glitch occurred during major sales events on Amazon and Flipkart, impacting users attempting to utilize their ICICI Bank credit and debit cards. Despite numerous complaints on social media, ICICI Bank has yet to release an official statement regarding the cause or resolution of the problem.

title: Without public dollars, Amazon fairgrounds development escapes Detroit's community benefits requirements
summary: The proposed Amazon distribution center at the former Michigan State Fairgrounds in Detroit is being developed without direct public incentives, a point touted by Mayor Mike Duggan. However, a community coalition argues that the city is effectively providing “backdoor subsidies” by selling the land below its appraised market value and covering environmental remediation and demolition costs, thereby sidestepping Detroit's Community Benefits Ordinance. This disagreement highlights concerns over whether the deal genuinely lacks public assistance and its implications for community engagement.

title: Miniso Raises $608 Million in U.S. IPO, MNSO Stock Jumped in Debut
summary: Miniso Group Holding Limited, co-founded by Chinese entrepreneur Ye Guofu and Japanese designer Miyake Junya, successfully raised $608 million in its U.S. IPO, with its shares (MNSO) debuting at $24.40 and closing up 4.4%. The company, backed by Tencent and Hillhouse Capital, stated its intent to use technology to stay ahead in the competitive retail market against giants like Amazon and Walmart. Ye Guofu, who owns an 80% stake, is set to become a dollar billionaire as a result of the listing.

title: Touchdown: Amazon is 'Project Super Bowl' tenant in KCK
summary: Amazon has been confirmed as the tenant for "Project Super Bowl," a 1 million-square-foot fulfillment center developed by Scannell Properties at the former Woodlands racetrack in Kansas City, Kansas. Amazon announced plans for two such 1 million-square-foot facilities in the Kansas City area, creating over 1,000 full-time jobs between Kansas City, Kan., and Park City. This development signifies a major industrial expansion in the region.

title: AWS and Carrier team up to combat food waste with analytics
summary: Amazon Web Services Inc. (AWS) and Carrier Global Corp. have partnered to create an analytics platform called Lynx, aiming to reduce food waste. Lynx will utilize AWS's cloud services to gather data from Carrier-made refrigeration units and other sources to monitor cargo, temperature conditions, and potential disruptions in the supply chain. This initiative seeks to improve the reliability and predictability of food transport and combat a significant global contributor to food waste by identifying and preventing spoilage.

title: ICICI Bank Is Down, Making Debit Card and UPI Transactions Fail for Many of Its Customers in India
summary: ICICI Bank customers in India experienced widespread issues with netbanking, debit card transactions, and UPI payments on October 16, 2020, with complaints peaking around 1:30 PM. The outage heavily impacted shoppers during major e-commerce sales by Amazon and Flipkart. Although the issue appeared resolved by the evening, some users continued to report errors, and the bank had not provided an official statement.

title: US small businesses hustle amid Amazon’s ‘Christmas creep’
summary: Small businesses are struggling to compete with Amazon after its October Prime Day event hastened the holiday shopping season amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. Many are urging customers to shop small and early, fearing another wave of closures. While some small businesses benefit from selling on Amazon, others worry that consumers will exhaust their holiday budgets before local shops can benefit, highlighting the ongoing economic challenges faced by independent retailers.

title: Garmin Vivofit Jr 3 vs Jr 2: fitness tracker for kids comparison
summary: This article compares the Garmin Vivofit Jr 3 and Jr 2, highlighting their differences in design, hardware, and functionality. The Vivofit Jr 3 has a larger, higher-resolution color display and looks more like a smartwatch, while the Jr 2 resembles a traditional fitness tracker with a smaller 8-color screen. Both offer similar activity tracking and parental controls, with the key distinction being aesthetic and minor feature additions like distance tracking and an ICE widget on the Jr 3.

title: Target to pay more than $70 million in bonuses to hourly employees ahead of holidays
summary: Target announced it will distribute over $70 million in employee bonuses, giving $200 to more than 350,000 hourly workers at stores, distribution, and contact centers ahead of the holiday season. This marks another round of bonuses during the pandemic, bringing Target’s total additional spending on employee pay and benefits to nearly $1 billion this year. The retailer's decision comes as daily new Covid-19 cases are rising and follows a strong fiscal second quarter with significant gains in sales and profits.

title: Whisk adds The Kroger Co. to Partner Ecosystem, Making Online Recipes Instantly Shoppable at Kroger Family of Stores
summary: Whisk, a Samsung Next food technology platform, has partnered with The Kroger Co. to allow consumers to turn online recipes into shoppable grocery lists for pickup or delivery from Kroger Family of Stores. This integration leverages Whisk's AI-powered Food Genome to ensure accurate product matching and inventory, streamlining the online grocery shopping experience for millions of Kroger customers, particularly as more people are cooking at home. The partnership enhances Kroger's digital ecosystem and expands Whisk's network of grocery retailers and content providers.

title: Microsoft and Elon Musk’s SpaceX partner to woo space customers
summary: Microsoft is expanding its cloud-computing platform into space by partnering with Elon Musk's SpaceX, connecting its Azure cloud to SpaceX's low-Earth orbiting satellites. This collaboration aims to give Microsoft an edge against rivals like Amazon and meet the increasing demand for data-heavy space services, such as disaster prediction and supply chain visibility. SpaceX hopes the revenue from its Starlink internet-beaming satellites will help fund its interplanetary goals and recently secured a $149 million Pentagon contract for missile-tracking satellites.

title: Database Case Studies with Cloud Volumes ONTAP
summary: This article showcases several case studies demonstrating how NetApp's Cloud Volumes ONTAP facilitates the migration and operation of various databases (SQL, MongoDB, Oracle, SAP HANA, Hadoop) in public cloud environments like AWS and Azure. Companies like Concerto Cloud, Mellanox, AdvancedMD, and Fujitsu achieved significant benefits such as reduced costs, improved data reduction, enhanced disaster recovery, and simplified data management by utilizing Cloud Volumes ONTAP for their cloud database strategies. The cases highlight the solution's ability to provide high availability, performance, and scalability across hybrid cloud architectures.

title: MongoDB Atlas now enables multi-cloud database clusters
summary: MongoDB has enhanced its Atlas cloud database service to support multi-cloud clusters, allowing databases to run simultaneously across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. This new capability addresses customer demand for data portability across different cloud providers, enabling features like live replication and proximity-based query routing for improved performance and compliance. The change shifts from running separate applications on different clouds to truly integrated, distributed databases across multiple cloud environments.

title: Friend Tire enters Florida market, leases industrial space
summary: Friend Tire Company, a subsidiary of Yokohama Rubber, has expanded into the Florida market by leasing a 46,020-square-foot industrial space in Four Corners Business Park in Davenport. The new facility will serve as a regional distribution center for the wholesale tire company, aiming to enhance its supply chain in the Southeast. Colliers International facilitated the lease transaction, highlighting the strategic location with excellent access to major interstates and key markets like Orlando and Tampa.

title: Detroit City Council approves sale of former state fairgrounds site for Amazon development
summary: The Detroit City Council has approved the sale of the former Michigan State Fairgrounds site for the construction of a 3.8-million-square-foot Amazon distribution center. This decision follows weeks of debate regarding the use of the publicly owned site for private development, with advocates citing job creation and productive use, while critics raised concerns about community benefits, environmental protections, and public access. The deal, valued at $9 million for the 142-acre site, is expected to create at least 1,200 jobs and includes a $7 million payment for a new public transit center.

title: FCA has hired 4,100 Detroit residents for its new Detroit Assembly Complex
summary: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV has successfully hired 4,100 Detroit residents for its new Detroit Assembly Complex, marking a significant investment in the city. This complex includes the first automotive assembly plant built in Detroit in nearly 30 years, creating 4,950 new jobs in total. The "Detroit at Work" program was instrumental in this hiring effort and will be leveraged for future projects, including Amazon's facility.

title: 9 Holiday Fragrance Sets Well Worth The Money (& A Spot On Your Wish List)
summary: This article highlights nine holiday fragrance sets for 2020, catering to various budgets and preferences, with options for both luxury brands and more affordable choices. It emphasizes that these sets make excellent gifts for beauty enthusiasts and perfume lovers, including offerings from brands like Dior, Chanel, Philosophy, and Ariana Grande. The selections range from mini fragrance collections and travel sprays to sets that combine perfume with other beauty products.

title: Nvidia’s A100 GPU sets new performance records in MLPerf benchmarks
summary: Nvidia's A100 GPU has set new performance records in the latest MLPerf benchmarks, dominating tests across six application areas for data center and edge computing systems. The A100 GPU significantly outperformed CPUs in image classification and recommender tests, demonstrating extreme cost efficiency benefits for AI inference. Nvidia's systems are also making an impact in various industries, including medical imaging, automotive, and financial services, and are integrated into powerful supercomputers.

title: WD-40 CEO reveals 3 of the craziest ways his lubricating spray has been used
summary: WD-40's CEO, Garry Ridge, highlights some unconventional uses for the company's famous lubricating spray, including deterring squirrels from bird feeders and freeing a burglar from an air conditioning duct. The article also notes the company's strong sales growth during the COVID-19 pandemic, attributed to increased home renovation activities. WD-40's fourth fiscal quarter saw a 5% increase in sales year-over-year, with significant surges in the Americas and EMEA regions.

title: Jakks Pacific recalls 'Skate & Skoot' scooters due to fall hazard, will provide replacement handlebar
summary: Jakks Pacific has recalled approximately 162,300 of its MorfBoard Skate & Scoot Combo scooters equipped with "Y" handlebars because the handlebar joint can break, posing a fall hazard. The recall affects scooters sold nationwide from February 2018 to August 2020. Consumers should stop using the "Y" handlebars and contact Jakks Pacific for a free replacement "T" handlebar.

title: Target's Black Friday plan: No early hours, more drive-up pickup spots
summary: Target Corp. is changing its Black Friday strategy for 2020 by canceling traditional early-morning store openings. The company is also promoting increased use of curbside pickup and implementing other measures to reduce store crowding during the Covid-19 pandemic. These changes aim to prioritize safety and adapt to evolving shopping habits.

title: Ball Corp. And Kroenke Sports Launch Expansive Partnership Including Denver Arena Naming Rights
summary: Ball Corporation and Kroenke Sports & Entertainment have announced a comprehensive partnership, which includes the renaming of Denver's Pepsi Center to Ball Arena. This deal provides Ball Corp. with a significant platform to promote its new recyclable aluminum cups across KSE's global sports properties, including the LA Rams and Arsenal F.C. The environmentally-focused partnership aims to boost aluminum recycling rates and replace disposable plastic cups with sustainable alternatives.

title: JD rolls out fleet of unmanned delivery vans after successful Wuhan test
summary: JD.com, China's second-largest e-commerce player, is deploying 100 autonomous delivery vehicles in Changshu by the end of the year, with plans for 100,000 "autonomous robots" over the next five years. This initiative follows successful Level-4 autonomous driving tests in Wuhan during the coronavirus lockdown, aiming to enhance customer experience and alleviate worker burdens. Analysts, however, caution that large-scale adoption could take over a decade due to high costs and the need for viable business models.

title: GSSC Series: JD Announces World’s First Level-4 Autonomous Delivery Vehicle Application at Scale
summary: JD Logistics announced the world's first Level-4 autonomous delivery robot application at scale in Changshu, Jiangsu province, with plans to deploy 100 robots by year-end. These robots operate unsupervised, planning routes and delivering packages, significantly improving efficiency for couriers like Jie Wang, whose salary increased by over 30%. This initiative highlights JD's commitment to advancing logistics technology and applying Level-4 autonomous driving to address the growing demand in China's delivery market.

title: Target bolsters coronavirus protections for shoppers ahead of holiday season hours
summary: Target is implementing new safety measures and expanding existing ones to protect shoppers during the upcoming holiday season amid the coronavirus pandemic. These changes include contactless payment options, online queue monitoring, increased mobile checkout devices, enhanced Drive Up services, and an extended Price Match Guarantee. The retailer will also be closed on Thanksgiving for the first time since 2011 and offer Black Friday deals throughout November.

title: Scannell Properties Plans Mixed-Use Redevelopment of Deluxe Corp. Campus
summary: Scannell Properties announced plans to redevelop Deluxe Corp.'s 49-acre Shoreview campus into a mixed-use development after acquiring it in a sale-leaseback deal. The Indianapolis-based company envisions a master plan including manufacturing, R&D, multi-family housing, and office-warehouse spaces, totaling around 500,000 square feet. Redevelopment will begin after Deluxe Corp. relocates its headquarters to downtown Minneapolis next fall.

title: SanDisk IXpand Wireless Charger Sync Can Also Backup Smartphone Data
summary: SanDisk, a Western Digital company, has introduced two new wireless charging accessories: the SanDisk Ixpand Wireless Charger Sync and the Ixpand Wireless Charger 15W. The "Sync" model offers integrated data backup for contacts, photos, and videos while charging, available in up to 256GB, ideal for users without microSD slots. The 15W model provides traditional fast wireless charging without the backup feature; both include safety features and come with a 2-year warranty, with the Sync starting at $99.99 and the 15W at $49.99.

title: Microsoft's SpaceX partnership sends Azure to the final frontier
summary: Microsoft has launched its Azure Space initiative, partnering with SpaceX to integrate Azure with low-orbiting satellites and introduce a new Azure Modular Datacenter (MDC). This move positions Microsoft to compete in the space and satellite segment of the IaaS market, particularly targeting telecommunications, government, and energy industries. The venture will put Microsoft head-to-head with AWS, which already has similar cloud-based space offerings, requiring both companies to address the persistent issue of latency in satellite communications.

title: If you suddenly can't print to your HP Printer from your Mac, you're not alone: Code security cert snafu blamed
summary: Many Mac users are unable to print to their HP printers due to a code-signing certificate issue affecting macOS Catalina and Mojave. Apple, via an XProtect update, revoked the certificate for HP's printer driver software, causing Macs to reject it as potentially damaging. HP later confirmed they "unintentionally revoked credentials on some older versions of Mac drivers" and are working with Apple to restore them, recommending AirPrint as a temporary workaround.

title: How Live Streaming Startup BeLive Went From Nearly Shutting Down To Hitting S$10M Revenue
summary: BeLive, a Singapore-based live streaming SaaS startup, pivoted from a struggling B2C model to a highly successful B2B model, achieving S$10 million in revenue. Initially facing cashflow issues and near closure, the company thrived during the COVID-19 pandemic by providing live streaming solutions to businesses. This strategic shift and increased demand for online sales platforms led to significant growth, employee expansion, and profitability.

title: AT&T Has The Most Disappointing Big Company Stock This Year
summary: AT&T Inc. (NYSE: T) has recorded the worst stock performance among large-cap companies this year, dropping 27% while the S&P 500 gained 7%. This decline is significant compared to top companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Facebook, which have seen substantial gains. The company also reported a 5% fall in operating revenue and a 22% drop in EPS, coupled with massive long-term debt, despite an impressive dividend yield.

title: How to invest in the S&P 500 without betting hard on the ‘FAAMG’ stocks that are 20% of the index
summary: This article discusses how to invest in the S&P 500 without heavily relying on the "FAAMG" stocks (Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com, Microsoft, and Google/Alphabet), which represent a significant portion of the index's valuation. It suggests that when investing in a standard S&P 500 index fund, one is implicitly making a large bet on the continued success of these five tech giants. The article hints at an alternative strategy, specifically mentioning an "Equal-weight S&P 500 ETF," for investors looking to diversify away from the concentrated influence of FAAMG stocks within the S&P 500.

title: How to invest in the S&P 500 without betting hard on the ‘FAAMG’ stocks that are 20% of the index
summary: This article discusses a strategy to invest in the S&P 500 without being overly exposed to the "FAAMG" stocks (Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com, Microsoft, and Google/Alphabet) which collectively represent 20% of the index's valuation. It suggests that when investing in a typical S&P 500 index fund, one is inherently making a significant bet on the continued success of these five dominant companies. The piece broadly hints at an "equal-weight S&P 500 ETF" as a potential solution for investors seeking diversification away from these outsized positions.

title: How to invest in the S&P 500 without betting hard on the ‘FAAMG’ stocks that are 20% of the index
summary: This article discusses a strategy for investing in the S&P 500 without being overly reliant on the performance of the dominant "FAAMG" stocks. It highlights that the FAAMG stocks (Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com, Microsoft, and Google/Alphabet) collectively represent about 20% of the S&P 500's valuation. The piece suggests that investing in an equal-weight S&P 500 ETF can mitigate the concentrated risk associated with these technology giants.

title: Gap To Dramatically Shrink Presence In Malls, Closing 350 Location In Next Two Years
summary: Gap Inc. plans to close 350 Gap and Banana Republic stores, primarily in malls, as part of a restructuring to shift towards e-commerce and off-mall locations. This move, which analysts predict will significantly impact locations like those in Rockland County, aims to make 80% of revenue come from online and off-mall sales by the end of fiscal 2023. The company will focus on its more successful brands, Athleta and Old Navy, while grappling with pre-existing sales slumps exacerbated by the pandemic and a lawsuit from Simon Property Group over unpaid rent.

title: Parade underwear: The co-founder determined to build a brand for Gen Z, by Gen Z
summary: Cami Téllez, co-founder and CEO of underwear brand Parade, discusses how the company is redefining the underwear market for Gen Z by focusing on social good, sustainability, and self-expression. Parade has achieved significant growth during the pandemic, surpassing 500,000 pairs sold within its first year and securing $8 million in funding. Téllez emphasizes the importance of community and aims for Parade to become a full-stack underwear company, extending beyond just bottoms.

title: Carter’s to close at least 200 stores
summary: Carter's plans to close approximately 200 stores, representing 25% of its fleet, as leases expire, focusing on more profitable e-commerce and wholesale partnerships. The closures target older, lower-margin stores in declining areas while the company also plans to open some new locations in densely populated areas. Despite the pandemic's challenges, increased e-commerce sales and essential children's apparel demand helped the company exceed third-quarter expectations.

title: Best WiFi extenders: Netgear, TP-Link, and Linksys win out
summary: This article reviews seven of the best WiFi extenders on the market to combat wireless dead zones. It categorizes top picks from brands like Netgear, TP-Link, and Linksys based on value, overall performance, power-user features, size, design, portability, and outdoor use. The guide also explains what WiFi extenders do, important specifications to consider, and their limitations compared to mesh WiFi systems.

title: Facebook, Google and Microsoft 'avoiding $3bn in tax in poorer nations'
summary: ActionAid estimates that Google, Facebook, and Microsoft are avoiding up to $2.8bn (£2.2bn) in tax revenue in developing nations, a sum that could significantly boost public services like healthcare and education. The charity is advocating for a new global tax system, ideally under the United Nations, requiring large corporations to pay a minimum tax rate based on their "real economic presence." This initiative highlights long-standing concerns about tech giants' tax contributions and their impact on global south countries, especially as these companies have seen soaring revenues during the pandemic.

title: These credit card offers can save you money or earn bonus points at electronics stores
summary: This article details how American Express cardholders can utilize Amex Offers to save money or earn bonus points at major electronics retailers like Best Buy, Dell, and Amazon ahead of Black Friday and the holidays. It explains how to stack offers, use gift cards to maximize promotions, and highlights specific offers such as additional points or statement credits. The author also suggests several Amex cards with high welcome offers for those looking to take advantage of similar future deals.

title: Utilimaster is Road Ready with Velocity F2, Class 2 Walk-In Van
summary: Utilimaster, a business unit of The Shyft Group, has launched its new Velocity F2, a purpose-built Class 2 walk-in van designed to meet the increasing demand in e-commerce and delivery services. Built on a Ford Transit chassis, the Velocity F2 offers a balance of nimbleness, comfort, fuel efficiency, and cargo capacity. It provides benefits such as lower total cost of ownership, no commercial driver's license requirement for operation, and improved fuel economy, with production orders now being accepted.

title: Election, Stimulus, or Rising Infections — What’s Driving Market Volatility?
summary: The ProShares Ultra VIX Short-Term Futures ETF (UVXY) spiked significantly on October 26th due to increased stock market volatility. This surge was attributed to concerns over rising COVID-19 infections, stalled stimulus talks, and upcoming U.S. elections and mega-cap company earnings reports. The article explains how the VIX Index and UVXY function in measuring and leveraging market volatility.

title: Apple shrinks, Amazon grows among Jabil’s largest customers
summary: Jabil's annual report shows a shift in its largest customer base, with Apple's share of revenue decreasing while Amazon's grows significantly. This diversification strategy aims to reduce Jabil's reliance on a single customer, a concern previously highlighted by analysts. The company also reported an increase in employees and manufacturing space, along with COVID-19 related costs.

title: Coca-Cola and AWS reimagine the future of contactless experiences
summary: Coca-Cola Freestyle partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to develop a "pour by phone" contactless experience for its beverage dispensers in response to evolving consumer behaviors during the pandemic. This innovation allows users to operate the machines via their smartphones by scanning a QR code, eliminating the need for physical contact. The solution was rapidly developed and deployed, and over 30,000 machines now have this touchless capability, with a full U.S. rollout planned by the end of 2020.

title: LG TV launches Shop Time app featuring QVC, HSN
summary: LG has launched its Shop Time app, a free shopping platform available on LG Smart TVs made between 2016 and 2020. The app allows users to purchase directly from retailers like QVC and HSN, offering tailored product recommendations and incentives like coupons for new customers. This initiative reflects a broader trend of companies, including Qurate Retail Group, experimenting with shoppable content on smart TVs and other digital platforms, especially accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Rackspace Technology Manages Basware Cloud Transformation with AWS Public Cloud Migration
summary: Rackspace Technology has successfully enabled Basware's cloud-native service delivery operating on Amazon Web Services (AWS) public cloud, significantly enhancing Basware's operational efficiency and security. This collaboration involved a migration to a fully AWS environment, the development of a robust automation framework, and securing enterprise discounts with AWS. The partnership has helped Basware reduce deployment times, accelerate the creation of testing environments, and halve its continuous integration spend through AWS Spot Instances.

title: Amazon Pay ICICI Bank credit card is fastest to cross 1 million milestone
summary: The Amazon Pay ICICI Bank co-branded credit card has rapidly surpassed 1 million cards issued in less than 20 months, becoming the fastest in India to reach this milestone. This success is attributed to its unique benefits such as unlimited rewards, instant issuance, direct crediting of points to Amazon Pay balance, and the introduction of a Video KYC facility. The card is now available to any registered Amazon India customer, including non-ICICI Bank clients, and offers various rewards and no-fee spending options.

title: Rackspace Technology opens new Singapore office
summary: Rackspace Technology has opened a new 4,876-square-foot office in Singapore's Central Business District, quadrupling its previous office size and anticipating a 25% increase in headcount. This expansion is part of the company's continued investment in the APAC region and its strategy to enhance digitization plans for businesses globally, especially for its cloud solutions following its IPO. The new office will serve as a base for expansion into ASEAN markets, focusing on helping businesses leverage cloud technology for efficiency, productivity, and cost optimization.

title: TForce Logistics Expands Operations in Toronto, Opens Third Distribution Center
summary: TForce Logistics has expanded its operations in Toronto by opening a third distribution center, a 21,000 square foot facility in Etobicoke. This expansion aims to enhance dedicated last-mile delivery capacity to support the surge in eCommerce volumes and demand for expedited final-mile services in the greater Toronto metropolitan region. The new center, along with existing facilities in Brampton and Markham, strengthens TForce Logistics' strategy of using multiple smaller facilities in dense areas to provide fast, flexible, and consistent delivery options for a wide array of goods.

title: Exclusive: Amazon confirms more new leases in New York City — and sources say there's more to come
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is set to open five new delivery stations in New York in the first half of 2021, with sources indicating that additional locations may also be planned. This expansion signifies Amazon's continued growth and investment in its logistics infrastructure within New York City.

title: Amazon bites into Apple's share of Jabil's revenues
summary: Amazon has significantly increased its business with St. Petersburg-based Jabil in 2020, becoming a larger customer. While Apple remains Jabil's biggest revenue source, Amazon's share of Jabil's revenues grew substantially this year. This indicates a diversification of Jabil's customer base.

title: As Kroger Restock winds down, questions remain over digital profitability
summary: Kroger's Restock strategy has significantly boosted digital sales and market share, but profitability concerns remain regarding its digital channels. The company is focusing on its Ocado tie-up and various productivity measures to narrow the margin gap between digital and in-store sales, acknowledging that the substantial investment in automated warehouses faces skepticism. Executives are optimistic about future growth, driven by shifts to at-home consumption and a growing digital media business.

title: McCormick & Co. to build 1.8 million square ft. distribution center in Sparrows Point
summary: McCormick & Company announced plans to build its largest distribution facility globally, a 1.8 million square foot Northeast Distribution Center, in Tradepoint Atlantic Industrial Park at Sparrows Point. The new facility is expected to be completed and operational by the second half of 2022. A groundbreaking ceremony is scheduled for November 12, with Governor Larry Hogan and Baltimore County Executive Johnny Olszewski slated to attend.

title: McCormick To Open New Distribution Center In Sparrows Point
summary: McCormick & Company, a Maryland-based spice company, is opening a new 1.8 million square-foot distribution center in Sparrows Point, Maryland, within the Tradepoint Atlantic Industrial Park. This facility will be McCormick's largest distribution site globally, aiming to increase capacity and meet growing demand for its products. The new center is expected to create more jobs and support Baltimore County's economic recovery, with an anticipated opening in the second half of 2022.

title: Netgear Orbi Pro WiFi 6 review
summary: The Netgear Orbi Pro WiFi 6 (SXK80) offers excellent WiFi performance over a large area, making it suitable for growing wireless networks in businesses. While it is easy to deploy and features a 6Gbps backhaul and tri-band AX6000 Mesh Router, its high cost makes it an expensive option compared to consumer-grade WiFi 6 hardware. The review suggests that for optimal performance and value, users should invest in a router with multiple satellites rather than a basic kit, and recommends the product for larger office environments rather than home use.

title: Online ordering surge fuels Sprouts' Q3 revenue growth amid pandemic
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market Inc. experienced a significant increase in online ordering during Q3 2020 due to changing consumer shopping habits amid the Covid-19 pandemic. The company's CEO anticipates e-commerce will continue to be a crucial component of its business strategy in the future. This surge in digital sales contributed to Sprouts' revenue growth for the quarter.

title: ARK Invest's Cathie Wood Reveals Her Successful Playbook
summary: Cathie Wood, founder and CEO of ARK Invest, shares her "playbook" for success, emphasizing thinking big, focusing on innovation, and embracing disruption. Her firm's impressive growth and the performance of its ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) demonstrate the effectiveness of her approach, which includes conviction in ideas, continuous brainstorming, curiosity, and collaboration with innovators. Wood also highlights the importance of making your own opportunities and the value of mentorship.

title: Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL) Probed by Germany Over Online Sales Curbs
summary: Germany's Federal Cartel Office is investigating Amazon.com and Apple over a policy known as "brandgating." This policy allows brand product manufacturers, like Apple, to have independent sellers removed from Amazon's platform if Amazon itself sells the items, raising concerns about potential antitrust violations.

title: McCormick to open distribution center in Sparrows Point
summary: McCormick & Co. Inc. announced it will open a 1.8-million-square-foot Northeast Distribution Center at the Tradepoint Atlantic Industrial Park in Sparrows Point, Maryland. This facility will be McCormick's largest distribution site globally, increasing capacity and leveraging advanced technology for improved efficiency. The new distribution center is anticipated to open in 2022 and will consolidate multiple warehouses, signifying McCormick's continued commitment to Maryland and the Baltimore region.

title: Amazon cloud revenue jumps 29%, in line with expectations
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) saw a 29% increase in revenue in the third quarter of 2020, reaching $11.60 billion, which was slightly below estimates. Despite this, AWS operating income jumped 56% to $3.54 billion, exceeding expectations and contributing significantly to Amazon's overall operating income. The growth was attributed to continued demand for cloud services during the pandemic, although other Amazon business segments grew faster this quarter.

title: ETF of the Week: Amplify Online Retail ETF (IBUY)
summary: This article features the Amplify Online Retail ETF (IBUY) as the "ETF of the Week." It highlights the significant growth in online retail, accelerated by the coronavirus pandemic, with IBUY showing impressive year-to-date performance. The article discusses projections for continued e-commerce expansion in the US and globally, contrasting it with the decline in traditional brick-and-mortar retail and predicting a strong online holiday shopping season.

title: Geojit Financial Services launches AI-powered global investment platform
summary: Geojit Financial Services has launched an AI-powered global investment platform in partnership with Stockal, a New York-based wealth management services platform. This new platform allows Indian investors to diversify their portfolios by investing in global equities, starting with US stocks and ETFs. The initiative aims to cater to the growing interest among domestic investors, high-net-worth individuals, and expatriates in global asset classes.

title: Add to cart: Amazon.com reports record profits amid pandemic
summary: Amazon.com Inc reported record profits for the second consecutive quarter and projected strong holiday sales, as the COVID-19 pandemic continued to drive consumers to online shopping. Despite incurring $4 billion in COVID-19-related costs for the current period, the company saw sales of $96.1 billion in the third quarter, exceeding analyst expectations. This surge in business has also brought challenges, including accusations of monopoly power and concerns over employee safety amidst the pandemic.

title: Marvell to buy Inphi in $10bn semiconductor deal
summary: Semiconductor company Marvell Technology Group is set to acquire Inphi Corp in a $10 billion cash-and-stock deal. The acquisition aims to strengthen Marvell's leadership in cloud infrastructure and expand its 5G presence, leveraging Inphi's expertise in fiber-optic data traffic and its customer base including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Facebook. This move is part of a broader trend of consolidation within the semiconductor industry.

title: Walmart launches new test stores to further blend tech and in-store ops
summary: Walmart has opened new test stores to rapidly experiment with omnichannel technology and processes, blending in-store and online operations. These stores aim to improve efficiency in areas like inventory management, order fulfillment, and checkout technologies. The initiative leverages Walmart's physical store assets to better serve both in-store and online shoppers, with a goal of making all eligible in-store items available online.

title: COVID recasts local landscape for game developers
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic is significantly reshaping Vancouver's video game industry, pushing companies to adapt to remote work and a more flexible approach to talent acquisition. According to Wil Mozell, CEO of Sun Machine Games, this shift necessitates that Vancouver-based companies leverage their tech strengths and adopt new operational models where talent can be located anywhere, rather than relying on in-office presence. The industry will increasingly focus on cohesive product development and efficiency rather than just the number of employees.

title: Black Friday: Jumia Nigeria Assures Consumers Cost-Saving Deals
summary: Jumia Nigeria's CEO, Mr. Massimiliano Spalazzi, announced that the 2020 Black Friday campaign, scheduled for November 6-30, 2020, will offer consumers significant cost-saving deals. The initiative aims to help Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) recover revenue lost due to the COVID-19 lockdown. Jumia, in partnership with various sellers and brands, will provide a wide range of products with special promotions, with an expected increase in sales volume throughout November.

title: Amazon.com Inc. announces construction of its first fulfillment center in ND
summary: Amazon.com Inc. announced the construction of its first fulfillment center in North Dakota, a 1 million-square-foot facility in Fargo. The center is expected to launch in 2021 and will bring over 500 full-time jobs to the area. Gov. Doug Burgum praised the innovation and the opportunity it provides for North Dakota small business resellers.

title: Analysis: In an epic pivot to the cloud, Microsoft makes Azure the linchpin of its future
summary: Microsoft's Azure cloud computing service is a central component of the company's innovation strategy, driving significant revenue growth and serving as a key differentiator from competitors focused on advertising. The company's overall financial performance is strong, with impressive growth across its three main business segments: Productivity and Business Process, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Microsoft's successful pivot to the cloud and its developer-centric approach have made it a leader in the tech industry, demonstrating remarkable spending momentum among its customers despite its large size.
